subject: biology
title: Non-specific human defences
key_idea: The body stops most pathogens getting in. The skin is a physical barrier. Mucus traps pathogens and cilia move it away. Tears and secretions contain enzymes (lysozymes) that kill bacteria. Stomach acid kills pathogens in food.

blocks.text: These defences work against any pathogen, so they are non-specific. This section covers the physical barriers.

items.meaning: A defence that works against all pathogens, not one particular type.
A sticky substance that traps pathogens.
Tiny hair-like structures on the lining cells of the airways. They move mucus along.

items: **Skin:** a tough, dry, dead outer layer that acts as a barrier. It is waterproof, so pathogens cannot get through.
**Skin oil (sebum):** oil on the skin surface repels pathogens.
**Scabs:** platelets help to form blood clots and scabs over cuts. These stop pathogens entering.
**Nose, trachea and bronchi:** these produce sticky mucus, which traps pathogens. Cilia move the mucus away from the lungs, towards the throat.
The skin is a barrier. Scabs cover cuts.
Mucus traps pathogens. Cilia move the mucus out of the airways.
Non-specific means it works against all pathogens.

blocks.text: Some defences use chemicals to kill pathogens. They are found in the stomach, the eyes and the skin.

items: **Hydrochloric acid** in the stomach has a low pH. It kills bacteria in food or in swallowed mucus.
**Lysozymes** are enzymes that kill some bacteria. They are found in tears, saliva and mucus.
Tears are antiseptic because they contain these enzymes. The skin also has glands that secrete lysozymes.

checks.q: Give two ways that the body prevents pathogens entering.
checks.a: Any two from: skin acts as a barrier, mucus in the trachea and bronchi or nose, cilia in the airways, hydrochloric acid in the stomach.

checks.q: State the function of ciliated epithelial cells in the airways.
checks.a: To move (waft) mucus (which contains trapped pathogens and dust).

checks.q: Describe how tears and stomach secretions stop pathogens infecting the body.
checks.a: Tears contain enzymes (lysozymes) that kill bacteria. Stomach acid (hydrochloric acid) breaks down or kills microbes.

exam_phrases: tears contain enzymes to kill bacteria

mistakes.wrong: The body prevents pathogens entering because white blood cells make antibodies.
mistakes.right: References to the immune response are ignored when asked how pathogens are prevented from entering. Give skin, mucus, cilia or stomach acid.

mistakes.wrong: Hairs in the nose stop pathogens entering.
mistakes.right: References to hairs are ignored. Say there is mucus in the nose that traps pathogens.

mistakes.wrong: The skin defends the body because scabs and clots form.
mistakes.right: Scabs and clots are ignored for this question. Say the skin is a physical barrier that stops pathogens entering, or that it produces oil or sweat.

worked_example.question: Mosquitoes carry a pathogen that causes malaria. Describe how the human body: prevents pathogens from entering, and defends itself against pathogens inside the body.
answer_points: Skin: a tough, dry, dead outer layer that acts as a barrier. Sebum / oil repels pathogens. Scabs form over cuts.
Stomach: contains (hydrochloric) acid, which kills bacteria in food or in swallowed mucus.
Eyes: produce tears, which contain enzymes to kill bacteria.
Breathing system: trachea, bronchi and nose produce sticky mucus that traps bacteria. It is carried away by cilia.
Inside the body: white blood cells engulf pathogens, and produce antibodies and antitoxins.
Memory cells are formed, which give a more rapid response if the pathogen re-enters.
worked_example.tip: A level 2 answer (4 to 6 marks) refers to both body defences and the immune system, with relevant detail.

mistakes.wrong: Cilia trap bacteria and stop them entering the body.
mistakes.right: "Stop bacteria entering" and "trap bacteria" are ignored for the function of cilia. Say cilia move or waft the mucus.

mistakes.wrong: Lysozymes are chemicals found in the stomach.
mistakes.right: Lysozymes are enzymes in tears, saliva and mucus that kill some bacteria. It is hydrochloric acid that is in the stomach.

worked_example.question: Describe how the physical barriers and chemical defences of the human body provide protection from diseases.
answer_points: Physical: mucus is produced by cells that line some surfaces, and traps pathogens.
Physical: cilia on lining cells of the respiratory system move mucus across the surface and move pathogens out of the body or into the throat.
Physical: skin is a thick, waterproof covering with dead cells on its surface, so pathogens cannot enter.
Physical: tears wash pathogens away. Blood clots or scabs cover wounds.
Chemical: skin glands secrete lysozymes. Lysozymes are enzymes in tears, saliva and mucus, and kill some bacteria.
Chemical: hydrochloric acid in the stomach has a low pH, which kills many pathogens.
worked_example.tip: For the top level, give more than one physical barrier and more than one chemical defence, and describe what most of them do.

exam_phrases: cilia will waft the mucus away from the lungs

mistakes.wrong: Nose hairs stop the virus entering the lungs.
mistakes.right: Nose hairs and other defence barriers are ignored. Say mucus from goblet cells traps the virus and cilia waft the mucus away from the lungs.

mistakes.wrong: Platelets produce antibodies and white blood cells clot the blood.
mistakes.right: Platelets clot the blood to prevent entry of pathogens. White blood cells produce antibodies to kill pathogens.

worked_example.question: Different parts of the body have natural defence mechanisms to stop pathogens infecting the body. These defences include: skin, tears, and secretions from the stomach. Describe how each defence stops pathogens infecting the body.
answer_points: Acid and enzymes break down microbes.
worked_example.tip: Name each defence and say what it does: a barrier, enzymes, acid.
